caption: grandpa broke the same lectern 300 times 📚
logline: A grandpa has broken the same librarian's lectern three hundred times, rerolling her book; ten years ago Grandma rowed to the island across the bay and told him to walk the water to her or stay, and this morning the book is Frost Walker II.
question: why tf has grandpa broken the same lectern 300 times?
premise: Grandpa has broken the same lectern three hundred times: the librarian holds up a book, he reads it, 'Not THAT one', and breaks the lectern again. His grandkid thinks he just hates that librarian. Grandma lives on the island across the bay; her window is lit every night (the kid: she's scared of the dark). He won't take a boat or build a bridge, ten years (the kid: he's so stubborn). When she left, rowing away, she told him: 'Walk the water to me. Or stay.' Mom says that means never.
twist: He's been rerolling the librarian for one book, Frost Walker (vanilla: breaking a librarian's lectern before you ever trade with her changes the book she offers; Frost Walker freezes water under your feet). Everyone, the kid too, heard 'never'; he took it literally. This morning the trade screen reads Frost Walker II, Grandpa says nothing, and he walks off the end of the dock as the sea freezes under every step, a white path toward Grandma in her lit window. Cut.

lines.text: My GRANDPA / has BROKEN / the same LECTERN / three hundred TIMES.
lines.say: My grandpa has broken the same lectern three hundred times.
lines.direction: amazed and fed up, one quick breath; the number lands

lines.text: The LIBRARIAN / holds up a BOOK. / He READS it. / Breaks the LECTERN / AGAIN.
lines.say: The librarian holds up a book. He reads it. Breaks the lectern again.
lines.direction: rhythmic, a routine the kid has watched a hundred times

lines.text: I think he just / really HATES / that LIBRARIAN.
lines.say: I think he just really hates that librarian.
lines.note: STANDARDS 0a: the kid's innocent misreading of the reroll (the lead's note: he REALLY hates that librarian)

lines.text: GRANDMA lives / on the ISLAND / across the BAY. / Her WINDOW'S lit / every NIGHT. / I think she's / scared of the DARK.
lines.say: Grandma lives on the island across the bay. Her window's lit every night. I think she's scared of the dark.
lines.direction: bright, a fact she likes, then a confident little theory
lines.note: 0a: the lit window misread (it's left on for him)

lines.text: He WON'T / take a BOAT. / Won't BUILD / a BRIDGE. / Ten YEARS. / He's SO / STUBBORN.
lines.say: He won't take a boat. Won't build a bridge. Ten years. He's so stubborn.
lines.direction: baffled and a little funny; the last word lands, eye-roll fond
lines.note: 0a: no boat, no bridge misread as plain stubbornness; 'bridge' is a thing he won't build: nothing to show, the open water is the picture

lines.text: When she LEFT, / she TOLD him:
lines.say: When she left, she told him:
lines.direction: leaning in, telling the family legend; straight into her line

lines.text: Walk the WATER / to ME. / Or STAY.
lines.say: Walk the water to me. Or stay.
lines.direction: stubborn, a dare, not teasing; the last word lands
matter-of-fact, a kid repeating what grown-ups say
lines.note: 0a: the kid takes Mom at face value

lines.text: This MORNING, / the LIBRARIAN / held UP / a NEW book.
lines.say: This morning, the librarian held up a new book.
lines.direction: quick, noticing; a lift on the key word; still not suspicious
surprised, a little slower, the last word held; not scared
lines.note: S09 holds through 'Grandpa didn't say' (his face, silent); the cut to S10 lands on ANYTHING
